question: According to SOCTA 2021, Europol’s most recent report, organised crime continues to extend its influence and networks in Europe by taking advantage in particular of the freedom of movement afforded it by the lifting of internal border controls. The report shows that 80 % of the organised crime groups operating in Europe use legitimate businesses as fronts to launder money, often across borders.

SOCTA 2021 also highlighted the fact that 40 % of criminals in Europe engage in more than one criminal activity. In view of the above, what steps will the Commission take to disrupt organised crime activities in Europe and eradicate these groups?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.3.2024) Organised crime is a significant threat to European citizens, business, and state institutions, as well as to the economy as a whole.

In response to the threats and challenges identified in the Serious and Organised Crime Threat Assessment (SOCTA 2021)1, the Commission has adopted the EU Strategy to tackle Organised Crime 2021-20252, which commits the EU to boost law enforcement and judicial cooperation, promote investigations that disrupt organised crime structures and tackle high priority crimes, work to eliminate profits generated by organised crime, as well as prevent their infiltration in the legal economy and society, and make law enforcement and the judiciary fit for the digital age.

The EU is currently implementing this strategy, as highlighted in the Sixth Progress Report on the EU Security Union Strategy3. Furthermore, the Commission has presented on 3 May 2023 a package4 of measures to strengthen the EU framework for fighting corruption5.

Most recently, in complement to the Organised Crime Strategy and the EU Drugs Strategy6 and Action Plan7, the Commission adopted the EU Roadmap on the fight against drug trafficking and organised crime8.

The EU Roadmap sets out 17 concrete, additional actions to enhance the resilience of logistic hubs against drug trafficking and criminal infiltration with a European Ports Alliance, to dismantle criminal networks, to promote crime prevention measures and to strengthen international cooperation.

The Commission together with the Belgian Presidency launched the European Ports Alliance public private partnership on 24 January 2024, bringing together a multitude of European ports, relevant industry associations as well as Ministers, relevant national authorities as well as EU agencies9.
